transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-04 15:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Marcus Reed (CTO, Helio), Priya Narang (Infra Lead), Leo Park (ML Eng), Sofia Kim (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): POC to validate latency SLO of 100-200ms p90 on medium-length prompts, cost targets, and behavior under bursty traffic. Need reserved baseline GPUs + burst nodes; fallback to smaller model/hosted path considered.

00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account; with me is Ravi our solutions engineer and Maya CSM. Marcus, thanks for squeezing us in.
00:12 Marcus Reed: yeah thanks, we've been looking forward to this. we wanted to scope the POC so we can validate perf and cost assumptions before committing to dedicated.
00:20 Jordan Lee: Great; high level goals from us - understand your traffic, agree success criteria, size reserved capacity for the POC, define burst strategy and explicit fallback policies, and schedule benchmark runs.
00:32 Priya Narang: Quick background: Helio runs a customer-facing assistant embedded in the product; current pre-prod load is around 60 RPS avg with spikes to 300 RPS during business hours. Latency target is p95 under 500ms but product team pushing for p90 200ms if possible.
00:52 Ravi Kapoor: ok that distribution matters a lot for autoscaling and KV-cash - sorry KV cache; the K-V cache hits will change GPU utilization. do you have sequence length and token mix?
01:02 Leo Park: median sequence ~120 tokens, 95th ~420 tokens for long form summarization flows. about 70% short prompt completions.
01:12 Jordan Lee: good, that helps. For the POC we typically recommend a reserved baseline to cover steady-state, plus burstable pool to absorb peaks. question: are you open to running the POC on Redwood Dedicated (reserved) or do you need private on prem?
01:26 Marcus Reed: We prefer Redwood Dedicated in cloud with VPC peering — procurement is faster than on-prem. Security team will need SOC2 docs and KMS integration.
01:36 Maya Ortiz: We can share SOC2 + security pack. KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated; for hosted there are different key management options.
01:46 Priya Narang: Ok, timeline — product team wants results within 6 weeks so they can decide on the Q2 roadmap.
01:52 Jordan Lee: Sounds doable; typical POC plan is 4-6 weeks: onboarding & config (week 1), benchmark runs + iterations (weeks 2-3), stability + edge-case tests (week 4), wrap + decision (week 5-6).
02:05 Marcus Reed: Success criteria: p90 latency under 300ms for standard prompts, p95 under 600ms for tail; cost per 1k tokens under $X (we'll fill number later), and no more than 1% error rate for model failures.
02:17 Ravi Kapoor: We'll define measurement harness - synthetic and replay of your real traffic. For capacity sizing we do model throughput tests to derive tokens/sec per GPU and recommend baseline reserve.
02:28 Leo Park: How granular is your autoscale? We worry about scale-up latency causing request queuing.
02:34 Ravi Kapoor: Our autoscale operates at the node/pool level with both fast warm pools for burst and gradual scale out. For Dedicated we can pre-warm GPUs as a burst pool with sub-minute warm times depending on the image and model. There's also continuous batching which increases throughput but adds a few ms to tail latency, we can tune batching thresholds.
02:51 Priya Narang: Pre-warm sounds good. Can you spell out fallback options if burst capacity isn't available due to quota?
03:00 Ravi Kapoor: Sure — three fallback strategies we use: 1) route to a smaller quantized model variant kept in the same pool (lower latency and cost), 2) route to a hosted/managed endpoint as best-effort (higher cost but more capacity), 3) queue with graceful degradation like truncated responses. We'll work with you to set policy precedence.
03:18 Marcus Reed: Any example numbers? if we reserve 4 GPUs baseline, and peak to 12 for burst, what's expected p90?
03:26 Ravi Kapoor: ballpark depends on model. For a 13B opt-like model we typically see 80-120 RPS per A100 equivalent with median prompt lengths; with continuous batching you might get higher effective tokens/sec but latency varies. We'll need to run a quick throughput sweep during the POC to give precise numbers.
03:44 Jordan Lee: We'll include those sample baselines in the POC SOW and run a initial perf sweep in the first benchmark window.
03:49 Leo Park: About cost—if we have reserved GPUs, do you allow burst billing only for the extra nodes? how's pricing modeled?
03:55 Jordan Lee: Reserved baseline is committed hourly; burst is pay-as-you-go with a premium per-GPU-hour. For Dedicated POCs we often include a limited number of burst hours in the POC credit. We'll send the pricing tiers in the SOW.
04:10 Priya Narang: Security asks: VPC peering, private subnets, SSO/SAML, audit logs. can you confirm retention windows for logs and where they live?
04:20 Maya Ortiz: yes, Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering and private subnets, SAML SSO via SAML2. Audit logs can be exported to your logging endpoint; retention configurable — we'll share the matrix.
04:30 Marcus Reed: Also need a runbook for incidents; e.g. if model stalls or KV cache thrashes.
04:35 Ravi Kapoor: we'll produce a runbook as part of the POC deliverables — includes tracing hooks, cache invalidation steps, circuit breaker thresholds.
04:44 Sofia Kim: For success criteria do you recommend synthetic tests or more replay from our real traffic?
04:48 Ravi Kapoor: both. synth tests help isolate baseline throughput; replay tests validate real-world patterns including session affinity and prompt mixes. If you can provide top-50 prompts and a traffic replay slice we'll use that.
05:02 Marcus Reed: We'll provide a 24-hour trace anonymized and a set of prompts. Priya will coordinate.
05:08 Priya Narang: yes we'll extract that. question — how do you measure tokenization differences across models? we use t5-tokenizer in house.
05:16 Ravi Kapoor: we usually normalize by token counts using the model's tokenizer; our harness accepts tokenization maps you provide so numbers align. some transcription stuff: our earlier doc said K V cash — apologies for that automated notes.
05:28 Jordan Lee: ok want to walk through an example POC config: baseline reserve 4 GPUs (A100 equiv), burst up to 12 for 30 min windows, fallback to quantized 7B variant, and route to hosted endpoint if still overloaded. Thoughts?
05:45 Marcus Reed: Sounds reasonable; 4 GPUs should cover steady 60 RPS. But if 300 RPS spikes last longer than 5 minutes we want to ensure no user-visible failures.
05:55 Ravi Kapoor: We'll set burst scaling policy to maintain latency SLOs for the first 10 minutes; beyond that automatic fallback to smaller model variant. We can also set request prioritization for internal vs external requests.
06:10 Leo Park: Does fallback change output quality? smaller model will degrade; must be flagged to product.
06:14 Sofia Kim: product needs a flag in responses so UI can show degraded quality.
06:18 Jordan Lee: absolutely, we can surface a response header or metadata field indicating model variant and fallback reason.
06:25 Priya Narang: For autoscale timings — what's your typical cold-start for a node? you said sub-minute but can you be more specific?
06:32 Ravi Kapoor: warm-image time for Dedicated is ~20-40s depending on model size; loading a model to GPU NVMe to memory could add 15-60s for very large models. That's why warm burst pools are recommended.
06:44 Marcus Reed: Benchmarks — we want p95 and p99 numbers too. can you include noise / variance measures?
06:50 Ravi Kapoor: yes, the benchmark report will include p50/p90/p95/p99 and standard deviation across runs, and a failure/error breakdown.
06:58 Jordan Lee: we'll propose 3 benchmark scenarios: 1) steady-state at 60 RPS, 2) burst profile 300 RPS for 10 minutes, 3) long-tail heavy tokens (95th percentile sequences). We'll run each and capture traces.
07:13 Priya Narang: Who will run the benchmark? do you need our credentials in their env?
07:18 Ravi Kapoor: we'll coordinate. For Dedicated POC we'll spin up a test VPC peered to your logging and use a runner within your network to replay traffic. you'll control keys and we won't persist logs beyond agreed retention.
07:30 Marcus Reed: Good. On procurement, we likely need a 6-8 week decision cycle. If POC shows positive we'll move to a quarterly reserved commit.
07:39 Jordan Lee: understood. We'll make the SOW explicit about deliverables and decision gates.
07:44 Leo Park: For the throughput sweep, can you show ops for quantized vs FP16? we have concerns about hallucination/regression with quantization.
07:53 Ravi Kapoor: we'll include FP16, int8 quantized (where applicable), and a mixed configuration. We'll also run quality evals on a known prompt set to check regressions and share diff metrics.
08:05 Marcus Reed: any risk of model variant incompatibility when falling back? like function calling or special tokens?
08:12 Ravi Kapoor: good point — function-calling behavior is model specific. We'll map capabilities across the variants and create compatibility rules in routing. If function-calls are required we can pin that route to a compatible variant only.
08:26 Sofia Kim: timeline — once we accept SOW how fast can you onboard the POC infra?
08:31 Jordan Lee: Usually 3-5 business days to provision Dedicated test pool and set up VPC peering windows (pending network approvals). Benchmark runs can begin after that.
08:40 Priya Narang: Network approvals are our slowest path. We'll try to expedite.
08:44 Marcus Reed: Anything else from Redwood?
08:47 Ravi Kapoor: we'll also provide a preliminary capacity spreadsheet with GPU throughput estimates per model variant. That will help you pick reserve numbers.
08:55 Jordan Lee: ok let's do a quick recap and assignments.
09:00 Jordan Lee: Recap — POC length 4-6 weeks, baseline reserve 4 GPUs, burst to 12 GPUs, fallback to quantized 7B variant and hosted endpoint; success criteria p90 < 300ms, p95 < 600ms, cost targets TBD. Deliverables: SOW + pricing, benchmark template, runbook, security pack.
09:22 Marcus Reed: Affirmative. We'll get you the traffic sample and top prompts by Thursday (2026-03-05).
09:28 Priya Narang: I'll send the infra diagram and peering windows (2026-03-05).
09:33 Jordan Lee: Great — Jordan will send SOW (2026-03-06), Ravi will share benchmark templates (2026-03-09), we schedule 2-hour benchmark week of 2026-03-16.
09:45 Maya Ortiz: I'll set up the calendar invite and include the runbook draft in the shared folder.
09:50 Marcus Reed: thanks everyone. good call.
09:53 Jordan Lee: thanks all, talk soon.
